chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Whoever turned away from right was ruined.

key_terms.صَفْحَتَهُ: his face/cheek (metaphor for turning away or showing one's face)
key_terms.لِلْحَقِّ: to the Truth (Al-Haqq, often referring to God or divine truth)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of turning away from the truth according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this concise maxim from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) warns that turning away from Al-Haqq (the Divine Truth) leads to spiritual ruin, reflecting the Shia understanding that truth is not merely intellectual but a transformative reality. This saying underscores the necessity of aligning one’s inner self with divine guidance, a theme central to the concept of *Imamah* as the anchor of truth in the post-Prophetic era. The warning serves as both a theological principle and a practical ethic for believers navigating the complexities of worldly life.
